claim: The StreamIndex repository states the implementation is tested on H100/H200 (Hopper, sm_90a) only, so running it on a CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80) is unvalidated even though Triton itself supports SM80.
stance_target: The assumption that the chunked CSA indexer can be dropped onto Ampere-class cards without porting work
scope_conditions: Repository README, requirements section; 2 commits, May 2026
quoted_support: Requirements: PyTorch >= 2.10, Triton >= 3.5, CUDA 12.x or 13.x, Python >= 3.11. Tested on H100 / H200 (Hopper, sm_90a).

claim: The repository's published result table confirms the paper's numbers: at S=32,768 the materialize path takes 317 ms and 129 GB while the chunked path takes 31 ms and 0.40 GB (10.3x), and at S=1,048,576 the chunked path runs in 30,900 ms at 6.21 GB peak.
stance_target: The claim that a chunked top-k makes CSA feasible at 32k on a 64 GB card
scope_conditions: Single H200 SXM, BF16, V4-Flash dimensions (H_I=64, m=4)

claim: The repository confirms the memory mechanism is the [B, S, H_I, T] FP32 score tensor materialized before top-k, which is 256 GB at S=65,536 with V4-Flash dimensions and exceeds the HBM of any single current GPU.
stance_target: The claim that the indexer step, not the attention kernel, gates sequence length
quoted_support: Public CSA implementations (V3.2-Exp reference, TileLang reference) materialize a [B, S, H_I, T] FP32 score tensor before the top-k reduction. With V4-Flash dimensions (H_I = 64, m = 4), that intermediate is 256 GB at S = 65,536, exceeding the HBM of any single current GPU.

claim: The repository is a minimal 2-commit project (May 2026) with raw benchmark logs committed under benchmarks/results/, so its numbers are reproducible but the codebase is young and lightly maintained.
stance_target: How much engineering risk adopting StreamIndex carries
